content.title: Gold Prices Climb Closer to $5,000 an Ounce
content.summary: Gold prices reached another all-time high Friday.    Most actively traded futures traded as high as $4,989.90 a troy ounce, an intraday record, before pulling back to about $4,983.   January futures settled at $4,976.

content.title: This Pro Is ‘More and More Bullish’ on Gold. How He’s Playing It.
content.summary: Gold  has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the financial and geopolitical ructions of the past year, vaulting from one record to the next and soaring nearly 80% from late last January, according to Dow Jones market data.  The events this past week surrounding the U.S. threats of a less-than-friendly takeover of Greenland were only the latest boost to bullion.  For instance, Goldman Sachs this past week hiked its year-end target to $5,400 an ounce from $4,900.

content.title: Gold Surges Over $4,800 to New High. Why It’s Leaving Silver Behind.
content.summary: Continuous gold futures  are up by 2%, climbing to $4,862.3 in early trading.  President Donald Trump will arrive in Davos later today for a showdown with European leaders, as his bid to seize Greenland threatens to tear the longstanding trans-Atlantic relationship apart.  For Mathieu Racheter, head of equity strategy research at Julius Baer, global markets have negatively “reacted to a fresh round of tariff rhetoric from Donald Trump targeting several European countries, accompanied by increasingly confrontational messaging.”
